mutants.why: J3: one batch of everything queued, one outstanding: a payment that cannot run takes the urgent ops down with it, and an outstanding payment batch delays them
J2: the batch reverts as a whole when a dispute op cannot apply (Depository today): the secret reveal in the same batch is lost with it
Q-J1: the Entity abandons all ops of a batch that reverted, but the signed batch can still land later
J2: the Entity does not read DisputeOpSkipped, so a skipped start stays pending: it waits for a DisputeStarted that never comes and signs the op again

mutants.why: F1: the fresh nonce ignores what is already signed, so a second batch with other content is signed at a nonce that one already holds; the adversary lands the old one and burns the new

R-SPLIT: a payment rides in the urgent batch; when it cannot run the mixed batch reverts whole and keeps its nonce open (J5 as built covers only a batch with no dispute, reveal or hash-ladder op), so the urgent op is lost with it and blocks every batch above it

J5: the failed batch is caught but the transaction still reverts, so the nonce write is lost and the nonce stays open (today's contract): it blocks every batch above it, urgent ones included, and F1 forbids signing other content at that nonce
E2: the chain accepts a nonce at or below the stored one, so a signed batch sent again runs its payment again
J5: the Entity does not read BatchFailed, so the failed payment is never queued again
